|28.13|Διαφέρει δ’ ἀλλήλων τό τε παράφωνον καὶ |28.14|ἀντίφωνον, τῷ τὸ μὲν παράφωνον ἀνισοχρό|28.15|νως συμφωνεῖν, ἠπίως πως καὶ εὐρύθμως |28.16|διαδεχομένων ἀλλήλοις τῶν φθόγγων ἀναλο|28.17|γίαις καὶ λόγοις καθ’ ὁμαλότητα· τὸ δὲ ἀν|28.18|τίφωνον ἰσοχρόνως, τοῦ ὀξέος τῷ βαρεῖ κα|28.19|τὰ ταὐτὸν συμφωνοῦντος, οἷον τοῦ ὀγδόου |28.20|τῷ πρώτῳ, τοῦ ἑνδεκάτου τῷ τετάρτῳ, τοῦ |28.21|δωδεκάτου τῷ πέμπτῳ καὶ τοῦ πεντεκαι|28.22|δεκάτου τῷ ὀγδόῳ, συνανιόντων ἢ συγκα|28.23|τιόντων ἐν ταῖς τάσεσιν ἢ ἀνέσεσι τῶν βα|28.24|ρέων τοῖς ὀξέσιν ἢ τῶν ὀξέων τοῖς βαρέσι κα|28.25|τὰ ἀνάλογον.

Ὁ δὲ τόνος καὶ τὸ ἡμιτόνιον |29.1|καὶ ἡ δίεσις, καθ’ ἑαυτὰ θεωρούμενα, ἀρχὴ |29.2|μὲν συμφωνίας, οὔπω δὲ συμφωνία. συμ|29.3|πληροῦται δὲ τὸ μὲν διὰ τεσσάρων ἐκ δύο |29.4|τόνων καὶ ἡμιτονίου καὶ μικρόν τι πρός, ὃ |29.5|καὶ διέσεως ἧττον ὂν προσωνυμίας οὐκ ἔτυ|29.6|χε· τὸ δὲ διὰ πέντε ἐκ τριῶν καὶ ἡμιτονίου· |29.7|τὸ δὲ διὰ πασῶν δι’ ἕξ· τὸ δὲ διὰ πασῶν |29.8|καὶ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων δι’ ὀκτὼ καὶ ἡμιτο|29.9|νίου· τὸ δὲ διὰ πασῶν καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε |29.10|δι’ ἐννέα καὶ ἡμιτονίου· τὸ δὲ δὶς διὰ πα|29.11|σῶν διὰ δώδεκα.

Λόγος δέ, τοῦ μὲν διὰ |29.12|τεσσάρων ἐπίτριτος· τοῦ δὲ διὰ πέντε ἡ|29.13|μιόλιος· τοῦ δὲ διὰ πασῶν διπλάσιος· τοῦ |29.14|διὰ πασῶν καὶ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων διπλα|29.15|σιεπιμερής· τοῦ διὰ πασῶν καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε |29.16|τριπλάσιος. οἷον, ὡς ἐπὶ ὑποδείγματος, |29.17|κείσθω πρῶτος ἐν ἀριθμοῖς ὅρος ὁ ἕκτος |29.18|ἡμῖν ἀριθμός· πρὸς ὃν πάντως ἐπίτριτος |29.19|ὁ ὄγδοος, ἡμιόλιος ὁ ἔνατος, διπλάσιος ὁ δω|29.20|δέκατος, διπλασιεπιμερὴς ὁ ἑξκαιδέκα|29.21|τος, τὸν ἕκτον δὶς ἔχων καὶ δύο μέρη αὐτοῦ, |29.22|τριπλάσιος ὁ ὀκτωκαιδέκατος, τετραπλά|29.23|σιος ὁ εἰκοστὸς τέταρτος.

⟨⟨Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς τὰ μὲν οὖν ἔμμεσα διαστήματα, οἷον τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων, τὸ διὰ πέντε μέλος, τὸ διὰ πασῶν, τὸ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, τὸ δὶς διὰ πέντε καὶ τὸ δὶς διὰ πασῶν, πρὸς τὸν προλαμβανόμενον φθόγγον τῶν λόγων ἔχουσι τὴν ἀναφοράν· τὰ δὲ ἄμεσα καὶ μεταξὺ τούτων κείμενα, οἷον ⟨ἡ⟩ δίεσις, τὸ ἡμιτόνιον καὶ ὁ τόνος, πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ αὐτῶν ἐγγὺς φθόγγους τὴν ποιὰν τῶν λόγων ἕξιν πεποίηνται· ὡς δὲ καὶ τὰ ἐκ συμφθάρσεως διαστημάτων πλειόνων μεγεθυνόμενα διαστήματα, οἷον ἡ τριδίεσις, τὸ τριημιτόνιον, τὸ διτόνιόν τε καὶ τριτόνιον καὶ εἴ τι ἕτερον τοιουτότροπον εἶδος, τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς κεκρυμμένων διαστημάτων πρὸς τοὺς ἐγγὺς φθόγγους πρότερον λογοθετηθέντων, οὕτως εἰς ἓν διάστημα ὡς ἐκ συμφθάρσεως κίρνανται. κατὰ σειρὰν μὲν γὰρ οἱ τῶν ἀμέσων διαστημάτων ἔκκεινται λόγοι, καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν δὲ οἱ τῶν ἐμμέσων, ὥσπερ ἐπὶ τῶν συλλογισμῶν αἱ προτάσεις καὶ τὰ συμπεράσματα· αἱ μὲν γὰρ προτάσεις ἐφεξῆς κατὰ σειρὰν οἷον πλέκονται, τὰ δὲ συμπεράσματα καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν τοὺς ἄκρους τῶν ὅρων συνδέουσιν. οὕτως οὖν ἔχει περὶ τοὺς λόγους καὶ τὰ τῆς μουσικῆς διαστήματα, τοῦ μὲν τῶν ἐμμέσων διαστημάτων λόγου καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν πρὸς τοὺς ἄκρους παραβαλλομένου τῶν φθόγγων, τοῦ δὲ τῶν ἀμέσων καθεξῆς πρὸς τοὺς ἐγγὺς ἀλλήλων φθόγγους συγκρινομένων, τῆς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐλαττόνων πρὸς τοὺς μείζονας προσαυξήσεως κατὰ σειρὰν προϊούσης, μονάδων μὴ τεμνομένων, ὅτι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς τοῦτο δέδοκται.⟩⟩

Εἰδέναι μέντοι |29.24|χρή, ὡς οὐ πρὸς τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν φθόγγων ἢ |29.25|τῶν χορδῶν οἱ λόγοι τῶν διαστάσεων κρίνον|30.1|ται, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὴν ἐπίτασιν τῆς ἠχῆς τῆς ἀπὸ |30.2|τοῦ βαρέος πρὸς τὸ ὀξύτερον.

departures.reason: Bas. stands alone against H Par. V. The witnesses write the enclitic with an accent (πῶς); ἠπίως πως, 'in a gentle way, as it were', qualifies διαδεχομένων naturally. πρῶτον ('first') has no witness and no counterpart in the description of the antiphonon that follows. The correction of the breathing (ἡπίως, a misprint) is orthographic only.

Bas. alone has δὲ. In H Par. V the last two items of the list of ratios are asyndetic (τοῦ … διπλασιεπιμερής· τοῦ … τριπλάσιος), and no witness, Bas. included, has δὲ at the next item (29.15). Bas.'s δὲ looks like a regularisation by the Basel edition.

δὶς is in the whole tradition at all four places where the compound consonances are named: H and V at 29.8, 29.9, 29.14 and 29.15, Par. at three of them, and Bas. itself at 29.8-9. Bas. is inconsistent: it keeps δὶς at 29.8-9 with Xylander's marginal 'abundant omnino, et delenda sunt' and lacks it at 29.14-15, presumably by Xylander's silent correction, which here coincides with Par. The same usage is in P's addition (τὸ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, τὸ δὶς διὰ πέντε as the fourth and fifth above the octave, referred to the first term like 16:6 and 18:6). So it is the tradition's own, non-classical name for the fourth and fifth above the octave (classical: διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων, Eucl. Sect. can. 12, Ptol. Harm. 1.5-6). By the editorial principle it is not to be classicised. Whatever is printed, the figures (8½ tones; 8:3 = 16:6) show that octave + fourth is meant. See the alternatives for translation.

Bas. stands alone. The tradition is consistent, as at 29.14: δὶς here belongs to the same usage as δὶς in 29.8-9 (Bas. included) and in P's addition. The figures (9½ tones at 29.10; 3:1 = 18:6) show that octave + fifth is meant.

In H, τὸ(ν) has the suspension stroke; V has τὸν. The masculine agrees with ὁ ἕκτος ἡμῖν ἀριθμός (29.17-18) and with the masculine ordinals used as numbers throughout: 16 'has the six twice and two parts of it' (12 + 4). The neuter τὸ ἕκτον would naturally mean 'the sixth part', which is wrong here. Bas. Par. probably derive from a copy whose abbreviation stroke was not read.

departures.Bas: — (passage absent; also absent from Par. H V)
departures.adopted: ⟨⟨Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς τὰ μὲν οὖν ἔμμεσα … ὅτι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς τοῦτο δέδοκται.⟩⟩
departures.source: P (Vinc. 340.7–342.4), with Vincent's corrections and two conjectures of this edition inside the passage (ἐκ συμφθάρσεως, twice; see apparatus); προσλαμβανόμενον is recorded as a conjecture only
departures.reason: P's fragment 2. Vincent places it after τέταρτος (Par. 24v.20, the 3rd line from the bottom). It is absent at this place from all the other witnesses, so it is printed in ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩ as a P-only passage. Its internal text was established from Vincent's print and his footnotes; see the apparatus and p_treatment.

departures.Bas: οὐ (printed οὒ, ου-ligature with breathing and grave)
departures.reason: Bas. stands alone against all the witnesses, and Vincent quotes the 1545 edition with ἢ. The sense is 'not by the number of the notes or of the strings … but by the tension'. The doubled negative οὐ … οὐ is unsupported and awkward. Compare the alternative 'of notes or strings' wording earlier in the treatise (εἴτ’ οὖν χορδῶν, Bas. p. 27, cited in the Bas. notes).

apparatus.entry: πως H Par. V] πρῶτον Bas.
apparatus.note: H Par. V all write πῶς with the circumflex (H 67r.1, Par. 24r.2, V 79r.3); printed as the enclitic. Bas. alone.

apparatus.entry: δὲ Bas. Par. V] γὰρ H
apparatus.note: H has a line-final 7-shaped compendium with a grave (67r.3), read γ(ὰρ); γ’ (= γε) is also possible. Either reading breaks the antithesis τὸ μὲν παράφωνον (28.14) … τὸ δὲ ἀντίφωνον.

apparatus.entry: βαρεῖ Bas. V] βάρει H Par.
apparatus.note: The difference is in the accent only, but it gives two words: the adjective βαρύς (βαρεῖ, paired with τοῦ ὀξέος, as the author pairs the adjectives at 28.23-24) and the noun βάρος, which in music means low pitch (LSJ s.v. IX; Theon p. 48 Hiller, in the definition of antiphony: τὸ ἀντικείμενον τῇ ὀξύτητι βάρος). H divides βά|ρει at the line end. Bas. prints βαρεί (acute), an accent misprint.

apparatus.entry: δὶς Bas. H Par. V] del. Xyl.
apparatus.note: Xylander's marginal note, keyed by asterisks to this δὶς and to the one in 29.9: 'abundant omnino, et delenda sunt'. δι’ ὀκτὼ καὶ ἡμιτονίου (8½ tones) = octave + fourth (6 + 2½). See departures 29.14-15 and the alternatives for translation.

apparatus.entry: δὶς Bas. H Par. V] del. Xyl.
apparatus.note: Same marginal note. δι’ ἐννέα καὶ ἡμιτονίου (9½ tones) = octave + fifth (6 + 3½).

apparatus.entry: τοῦ διὰ πασῶν H Par. V] τοῦ δὲ διὰ πασῶν Bas.
apparatus.note: Bas. alone. No witness has δὲ at the next item (29.15).

apparatus.entry: καὶ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων H V] καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων Bas. Par.
apparatus.note: Bas.'s omission here and at 29.15 is presumably Xylander's correction, in line with his marginal note at 29.8-9; Par. already lacks δὶς here. The ratio διπλασιεπιμερής (8:3, exemplified 16:6) fits octave + fourth.

apparatus.entry: καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε H Par. V] καὶ διὰ πέντε Bas.
apparatus.note: In Par. a stop stands after πασῶν (24v.10); this is punctuation only. The ratio τριπλάσιος (3:1, exemplified 18:6) fits octave + fifth.

apparatus.entry: τὸν H V] τὸ Bas. Par.
apparatus.note: H τὸ(ν) with the suspension stroke expanded; V ⟦r Τ⟧ὸν with a red initial at the line beginning.

apparatus.entry: ⟨⟨Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς τὰ μὲν οὖν ἔμμεσα … τοῦτο δέδοκται⟩⟩ P (Vinc. 340.7–342.4)] om. Bas. H Par. V
apparatus.note: Vincent's placement: 'à intercaler à l’édition de 1545, au fol. 24 vers. l. 3 en montant, après le mot τέταρτος'. In P it is followed by P's form of Bas. 29.23-25; see below. The next eight entries concern the text of this passage, for which only P (as reported), Vincent's corrections and conjectures exist.

apparatus.entry: μέλος P (Vinc.), kept] {μέλος} del. fort.
apparatus.note: μέλος is unexpected in a list of intervals; kept as the author's word for a sung span (cf. 27.12). Decided 4 : 1 (30.10.2026); deletion proposed by one judge.

apparatus.entry: προλαμβανόμενον P] προσλαμβανόμενον coni. (fort. recte)
apparatus.note: Vincent prints προ-|λαμβανόμενον, divided at his line end, without a note. προσλαμβανόμενος is the author's own name for the first note of the system (25.4–5, all witnesses), and the ἔμμεσα listed here (fourth, fifth, octave, δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, δὶς διὰ πέντε, double octave) are exactly the intervals from that note: the base term 6 of the example (29.17–23) stands for note 1, and 8, 9, 12, 16, 18, 24 for notes 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 15 (cf. 28.19–22). A single σ lost after πρὸς τὸν, in P or in Vincent's print. See doubts and alternatives.

apparatus.entry: ⟨ἡ⟩ δίεσις Vinc.] δίεσις P (ut vid.)
apparatus.note: Vincent prints [ἡ] without a footnote; his square brackets most probably mark his own supplement, so P lacks ἡ. Athetesis cannot be excluded, in which case P has ἡ. Printed in angle brackets, for parallelism with τὸ ἡμιτόνιον καὶ ὁ τόνος and with Bas. 28.25-29.1 (ὁ τόνος καὶ τὸ ἡμιτόνιον καὶ ἡ δίεσις).

apparatus.entry: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως coni.] ἐξυφθάρσεως P | ἐξ φθάρσεως Vinc.
apparatus.note: Vinc. n. 2: 'Ms. ἐξυφθάρσεως. — Ces mots sont inconnus aux dictionnaires.' Vincent's division gives neither a grammatical phrase (ἐξ before φ) nor sense. ἐκ συμφθάρσεως is the author's own phrase, in the same sense and with the same ἓν … διάστημα: ὡς ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (27.10), ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως διάστημα (32.10–11), ἓν διτόνιον ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (32.17). The corruption needs only the phonetic spelling ἐξ- for ἐκ σ- and the loss of μ before φ; every letter of -υφθάρσεως is kept. P garbles the same word in fr. 1 (σύμφρασις for σύμφθαρσις, after 27.14). See doubts.

apparatus.entry: διαστημάτων Vinc.] διαστήματα P
apparatus.note: Vinc. n. 3. The genitive is required after the preceding noun in -σεως: 'composed of several intervals'. P's accusative repeats the following διαστήματα.

apparatus.entry: κεκρυμμένων P] κεκραμένων Vinc.
apparatus.note: Vinc. n. 4 gives 'Ms. κεκρυμμένων'. P's reading, 'the intervals contained (latent) in them', gives good sense, so it is kept. Vincent's κεκραμένων echoes κίρνανται at the end of the sentence. See alternatives.

apparatus.entry: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως coni.] ἐξυφθάρσεως P | ἐξ φθάρσεως Vinc.
apparatus.note: Same as at 340.13-14 (Vinc. n. 2 refers to both places): εἰς ἓν διάστημα ὡς ἐκ συμφθάρσεως κίρνανται, 'are blended into one interval as by fusion'.

apparatus.entry: ἐμμέσων coni.] ἐν μέσῳ P (Vinc.)
apparatus.note: Vincent prints ἐν μέσῳ without a note. The class is called ἔμμεσα at 340.7 and τῶν ἐμμέσων at 340.25; ἐν μέσῳ would rather describe the ἄμεσα (340.11). The same confusion at Bas. 31.10 (ἐμμέσω H : ἐν μέσῳ Bas. Par. V). Decided by the judges 4 : 1 (30.10.2026); see resolved doubts.

apparatus.entry: μονάδων Vinc.] μονάδος P
apparatus.note: Vinc. n. 1. P's singular does not agree with τεμνομένων. The other possible remedy would be μονάδος μὴ τεμνομένης.

apparatus.entry: ὅτι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς τοῦτο P] ὅ, τι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς οὔ πω Vinc.
apparatus.note: Vinc. nn. 2-3 give 'Ms. ὅτι', 'Ms. τοῦτο'. P's text is sound: 'since not even the arithmeticians have accepted this', that is, the division of the unit. Vincent's change creates a doubled negative (μηδὲ … οὔ πω).

apparatus.entry: Εἰδέναι μέντοι χρή, ὡς οὐ Bas. H Par. V] Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς P (Vinc. 342.5)
apparatus.note: This is P's form of the sentence, at the same place (Vinc. 342.5-6). Vincent adds the edition's text for comparison: 'Éd. Εἰδέναι μέν τοι χρὴ, ὡς οὐ πρὸς τὸν ἀ. τ. φ. ἢ τ. χ.'. In these notes his practice is to quote the edition's divergent words (340.3 'Éd. παρά'; 342.25-26 'Éd. τῶν δὲ διαστημάτων'). Here he writes out Εἰδέναι μέν τοι χρὴ, ὡς οὐ in full and abbreviates only the words that agree (ἀ. τ. φ. ἢ τ. χ.). So the absence of οὐ is most probably P's reading as Vincent read it, not a slip in his print, and P's ἢ is confirmed. Without οὐ the sentence reverses the sense ('the ratios … are judged by the number of the notes or of the strings'). Vincent breaks off after κρίνονται with κ. τ. λ., so it is not known whether P went on with ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὴν ἐπίτασιν …. P agrees with the other witnesses from πρὸς τὸν ἀριθμὸν to κρίνονται and is not reported after κρίνονται. H's μέν|⟦r Τ⟧οι is μέντοι divided across the line (orthographic).

apparatus.entry: ἢ H Par. V P] οὐ Bas.
apparatus.note: Bas. prints the ου-ligature with breathing and accent (transcribed οὒ); Bas. alone. Vinc. quotes Éd. 1545 with ἢ.

orthographica.Bas: Word division: 28.13 τότε for τό τε (printed as one word, with the accent of τό; as printed it would be the adverb 'then', but the difference is only a missing space); ἐπείτοιγε (30.2, after the end of the section). Breathings and accents: 28.15 ἡπίως (rough breathing, misprint) for ἠπίως; 28.18 βαρεί (acute) for βαρεῖ; 28.19 ταυτὸν without coronis for ταὐτόν; 28.25 capital Ο without breathing for Ὁ; the grave is regularly set before commas and stops (29.4 πρὸς, 29.5 ὂν, 29.15 διπλασιεπιμερὴς·, 29.18 ἀριθμὸς., 29.24 χρὴ,), normalised. Spelling: 29.19 ἔννατος (also Par.), normalised ἔνατος (H V). 28.18 τοῦ ὀξέως as a genitive (so all witnesses), normalised ὀξέος, since the same text has τοῦ βαρέος (30.2) in all witnesses; if the editor prefers to keep the unanimous form, read ὀξέως. 29.20 ἑξκαιδέκατος (all witnesses) is kept as the text's Byzantine form, not changed to ἑκκαιδέκατος. Elisions δ’, καθ’, δι’ as in all witnesses; κατὰ ἀνάλογον (28.24-25) is unelided in all witnesses and kept. Capitals: Συμ- (29.2) after a full stop is lowercased; capitals are kept only at the run-in section breaks, which Bas. marks by extra space (28.25 Ὁ, 29.11 Λόγος, 29.23 Εἰδέναι); these begin new paragraphs, as does P's Σκοπητέον. Xylander's reference asterisks before δὶς (29.8, 29.9), keyed to his marginal note, are not reproduced. Punctuation is redone for sense.
orthographica.H: Iota subscript is mostly omitted (τῶ, πρώτω, τετάρτω, πέμπτω), but adscript in τῶι (67r.6, 67r.7) and ὀγδόωι (67r.8); the machine's 'check' entries there are orthographic. Word division: τό, τε (66v.21, comma-like sign = hypodiastole); διαπέντε, διαπασῶν, διαπασῶν written as one word (67r.18-19); μέν|τοι divided at the line end, with a red initial Τ at 67v.15 (the ekthesis initial of the first full line of the paragraph Εἰδέναι …, not a variant); ἐπεί τοι γε (67v.19, after the section). Accents and breathings: πῶς (67r.1) for the enclitic πως; βά|ρει (67r.4-5; see apparatus); ἠπίως correct; line-final τοῦ without accent (67r.5); accent of δίεσις placed between ι and ε (67r.12); ταυτὸν without coronis; διπλασιεπιμερὴς with grave before a stop (67v.11). Spelling: ἔνατος; τοῦ ὀξέως as genitive (as all witnesses); ἑξκαιδέκατος. συνανιόντων is written with a μ-like first nasal (67r.8). Abbreviations expanded: (καὶ) 67r.7, 67r.16; γ(ὰρ) 67r.3 (see apparatus); τὸ(ν) 67v.11 (see apparatus). A red initial Ὁ (67r.12) marks the new paragraph Ὁ δὲ τόνος. Punctuation: frequent high and low points between terms and numbers (e.g. τοῦ ἑνδεκάτου. τῶ τετάρτω·; ἐπίτριτος, ὁ ὄγδοος. ἡμιόλιος. ὁ ἔνατος·); not followed.
orthographica.P: Known only from Vincent's print (Vinc. 340.7–342.6); his accents, punctuation and capitals (Σκοπητέον, Κατὰ, Οὕτως; grave before commas, e.g. καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν δὲ,) are his own and are normalised. Vinc. n. 5 to 340.23 records Ms. καθυπ. (abbreviation) for καθ’ ὑπερβατόν, an expansion and not a variant. Vinc. n. 2: the Ms. writes ἐξυφθάρσεως as one word (emended to ἐκ συμφθάρσεως; see apparatus). Vincent prints ὅ, τι with hypodiastole and οὔ πω divided (his conjecture; see apparatus). κίρνανται is kept as printed; προλαμβανόμενον (340.9-10) is emended to προσλαμβανόμενον (see apparatus).
orthographica.Par: τό, τε with hypodiastole (23v.21); ἐνδεκάτου with smooth breathing (24r.8); ἠπίως correct; πῶς accented for the enclitic πως (24r.2); βάρει (24r.6; see apparatus); ταυτὸν without coronis. Acute before punctuation (δέ, 24r.18; πρός. 24r.20; ὄν, 24r.21; χρή, 24v.20; διπλασιεπιμερής. 24v.9), and acute kept before the following word in διπλασιεπιμερής ὁ (24v.16). Spelling: ἔννατος (24v.15); τοῦ ὀξέως as genitive; ἑξκαιδέκατος. ἐπείτοιγε as one word (25r.3, after the section). Sentence beginnings are in lower case. Heavy punctuation with stops and high points inside syntactic units, not followed (e.g. ὁ δὲ τόνος. καὶ τὸ ἡμιτόνιον· 24r.14-15; ἐκ δύο τόνων· καὶ ἡμιτονίου. 24r.19; τοῦ διὰ πασῶν. καὶ δὶς 24v.10).
orthographica.V: τό τε (78v.21); ἠπίως correct; πῶς with circumflex (79r.3) for the enclitic πως; βαρεῖ correct (79r.7); ταυτὸν without coronis. Spelling: ἔνατος; τοῦ ὀξέως as genitive; ἑξκαιδέκατος. Syllable division before γγ/γμ (φθό|γγων 79r.4-5, ὑποδεί|γματος 79v.14-15). Red initials at line beginnings mark the first full line of a new sentence or paragraph and are not variants: ⟦r κ⟧αὶ 79r.11, ⟦r Τ⟧ὸ 79r.19, ⟦r Τ⟧οῦ 79v.13, ⟦r Τ⟧ὸν 79v.21, ⟦r ὡ⟧ς 80r.4. Colon-like stops are used as strong punctuation (79r.15, 79v.7, 80r.3). ἐπείτοι (80r.8, after the section).

doubts.issue: The list of ratios ends with the octave + fifth (τριπλάσιος), although the list of intervals just before it ends with the double octave (τὸ δὲ δὶς διὰ πασῶν διὰ δώδεκα, 29.10-11). The numerical example also goes on to τετραπλάσιος ὁ εἰκοστὸς τέταρτος (29.22-23), and P's addition counts the double octave among the intervals referred to the first term. A clause «τοῦ δὲ δὶς διὰ πασῶν τετραπλάσιος» may have fallen out by homoeoteleuton (τρι-πλάσιος … τετρα-πλάσιος).
doubts.options: (a) Keep as transmitted (adopted). (b) Mark a lacuna *** after τριπλάσιος. (c) Supply ⟨τοῦ δὲ δὶς διὰ πασῶν τετραπλάσιος⟩ (conjecture).
doubts.evidence: All witnesses (Bas. Par. H V) agree on the shorter list, so the omission, if it is one, is older than H (1040). The author may simply have let the example run one step further than the list. Not decidable; kept.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: τὸ διὰ πασῶν καὶ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων / τὸ διὰ πασῶν καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: τὸ διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων / τὸ διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ πέντε (δὶς deleted)
alternatives_for_translation.witnesses: Xyl. (marg. at 29.8-9: 'abundant omnino, et delenda sunt'); Bas. at 29.14-15; Par. at 29.14
alternatives_for_translation.why: Whichever reading is printed, the intervals meant are the octave plus a fourth (8½ tones; 8:3, exemplified 16:6) and the octave plus a fifth (9½ tones; 3:1, exemplified 18:6). They are not 'the octave and twice the fourth/fifth', which would be 11 and 13 tones (32:9 and 9:2). The translator should render δὶς here as marking the fourth/fifth 'again', in the second octave (as in P's τὸ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων), with a note, and not as a multiplier. Xylander's text without δὶς gives the classical names.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: ἠπίως πως καὶ εὐρύθμως ('in a gentle, as it were, and rhythmical way')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: ἠπίως πρῶτον καὶ εὐρύθμως ('first gently and rhythmically')
alternatives_for_translation.why: This is the Basel reading, which translations made from Bas. will follow; it is weaker but not absurd.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: πρὸς τὸν προλαμβανόμενον φθόγγον ('to the note taken first', i.e. the base term of the example; P as reported)
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: πρὸς τὸν προσλαμβανόμενον φθόγγον ('to the proslambanomenos', the lowest note of the system; conjecture)
alternatives_for_translation.witnesses: conjecture (the adopted reading is P as printed by Vinc.)
alternatives_for_translation.why: Either way the same note is meant, the 1st of the fifteen notes counted in Bas. 28.19-22 and the base term 6 of the example. If the human editor keeps P's form, the translator may still name the note and give the technical term in a note.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς κεκρυμμένων διαστημάτων ('the intervals contained, latent, in them')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς κεκραμένων διαστημάτων ('the intervals mixed in them')
alternatives_for_translation.why: Vincent's correction echoes κίρνανται ('are blended') at the end of the sentence. Both give good sense.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως ('by the fusion of several intervals' / 'as by fusion'; conjecture)
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: †ἐξυφθάρσεως† (P; untranslatable as it stands); ἐξ φθάρσεως ('from dissolution', Vinc.); or conj. ἐκ συνθέσεως ('by the composition of several intervals' / 'as by composition')
alternatives_for_translation.why: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως is the author's own phrase (27.10, 32.10–11, 32.17) and is printed. If the human editor restores the obeli, the context (tridiesis, trihemitone, ditone, tritone as intervals made up of several smaller ones and 'blended into one') still gives the sense 'fusion' or 'composition'.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: ὅτι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς τοῦτο δέδοκται ('since not even the arithmeticians accept this')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: ὅ, τι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς οὔ πω δέδοκται ('a thing that not even the arithmeticians have yet accepted')
alternatives_for_translation.why: Vincent's printed text, which readers of Vincent will know. The sense is nearly the same.

sections.p_treatment: P fragment 2 (Vinc. 340.7–342.4) is printed in ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩ inside Bas. 29.23, after «τέταρτος.» and before «Εἰδέναι», at the place Vincent gives (Par. 24v, 3rd line from the bottom). The base for its text is Vincent's print, with P's manuscript readings taken from his footnotes. P's reading is kept wherever it gives sense: κεκρυμμένων (Vinc. κεκραμένων); ὅτι … τοῦτο (Vinc. ὅ, τι … οὔ πω). Vincent's corrections are adopted where P is ungrammatical: διαστημάτων for διαστήματα; μονάδων for μονάδος. The unexplained ἐξυφθάρσεως (twice; Vinc. ἐξ φθάρσεως) is obelized. Vincent's bracketed [ἡ] is printed as ⟨ἡ⟩. Ms. καθυπ. is treated as an abbreviation of καθ’ ὑπερβατόν. P's next sentence (Vinc. 342.5-6, «Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς πρὸς τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν φθόγγων ἢ τῶν χορδῶν, οἱ λόγοι τῶν διαστάσεων κρίνονται») is P's form of Bas. 29.23-25, so it is not inserted. It goes into the apparatus as two variants: «Σκοπητέον δὲ ὡς» against «Εἰδέναι μέντοι χρή, ὡς οὐ»; and ἢ, where P agrees with H Par. V against Bas. οὐ. Vincent breaks off with κ. τ. λ. after κρίνονται, so P is cited as extant only up to that word. P's use of «τὸ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, τὸ δὶς διὰ πέντε» for the 11th and 12th is also cited in support of keeping δὶς at 29.8-15.

resolved_doubts.issue: Check of the harmonic content. The tone counts (fourth 2 tones + semitone + 'something small'; fifth 3 + semitone; octave 6; octave + fourth 8½; octave + fifth 9½; double octave 12) and the ratios and example numbers (6 : 8 : 9 : 12 : 16 : 18 : 24, giving 4:3, 3:2, 2:1, 8:3, 3:1, 4:1) agree in all witnesses and with each other. Two points are the author's own and are not to be emended. First, the fourth is said to exceed two tones and a semitone by an unnamed remainder smaller than a diesis, whereas Pythagorean theory makes it smaller than 2½ tones (Euclid, Sect. can. 15). Second, 8:3 is called by the generic name διπλασιεπιμερής (the specific name in Nicomachus' classification is διπλασιεπιδιμερής).
resolved_doubts.options: Keep everything as transmitted (adopted); the translator should note it rather than correct it.
resolved_doubts.evidence: There is no variant in any witness at these places. «τὸν ἕκτον δὶς ἔχων καὶ δύο μέρη αὐτοῦ» = 16 = 2 × 6 + 4 (two thirds of 6), correct.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 5 : 0: Both points kept as the author wrote them (the fourth as two tones, a semitone and 'something small'; διπλασιεπιμερής for 8:3), to be explained in the translator's note. Theon of Smyrna p. 56.13-14 Hiller calls 8:3 πολλαπλασιεπιμερής, διπλάσιος γὰρ καὶ διεπίτριτος; the leftover in the fourth reflects the Platonic leimma (Theon pp. 67, 75).

resolved_doubts.issue: ἐξυφθάρσεως (Ms., twice) is not a known word, and Vincent's ἐξ φθάρσεως is neither grammatical (ἐξ before φ) nor meaningful in context ('intervals enlarged … of several intervals'; 'blended into one interval as by …').
resolved_doubts.options: (a) †ἐξυφθάρσεως† (the editor's text). (b) ἐξ φθάρσεως (Vinc.). (c) ἐκ συνθέσεως (editor's conjecture: 'by composition of several intervals'; the passage is about composite intervals, and fragment 1 ends on ἀσύνθετα διαστήματα; ἐκ σ- may have been written ἐξ-). (d) ἐξ ὑφάνσεως (editor's conjecture: 'as by a weaving'; closer to the letters ἐξυφ-, and cf. πλέκονται in the same passage). (e) ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (reviewer's conjecture, printed by the arbiter's decision: 'the intervals enlarged by the fusion of several intervals'; 'are blended into one interval as by fusion'). LSJ s.v. σύμφθαρσις: the joint destruction of the components of a mixture when a new body is produced from them (Alex. Aphr. Mixt. 216.24), and the 'melting into one another' of things (Hermog. Id. 1.12; cf. Iambl. in Nic. p. 80 Pistelli). This is the sense required by κίρνανται and εἰς ἓν διάστημα.
resolved_doubts.evidence: Vinc. n. 2 is the only report of the manuscript. (c) and (d) are not palaeographically compelling. (e) keeps every letter of the transmitted -υφθάρσεως and requires only the phonetic spelling ἐξ- for ἐκ σ- (κσ = ξ) and the loss of μ before φ: ἐκ συ(μ)φθάρσεως > ἐξυφθάρσεως. Vincent's ἐξ φθάρσεως already isolates the stem. Decisive for (e): the phrase is the author's own, with the same ἓν … διάστημα: ὡς ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (27.10), ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως διάστημα (32.10–11), ἓν διτόνιον ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (32.17); and P's fr. 1 (printed after 27.14) argues about the same σύμφθαρσις, which P garbles there too (σύμφρασις, emended in the same way). Printed as a conjecture of this edition; the human editor may prefer to keep the obeli.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 in the cross-check of the 25 places: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (conjecture; all four judges).

resolved_doubts.issue: In «τὸ διὰ πέντε μέλος» the word μέλος is out of place in a list of interval names. It may be a corruption (of an abbreviation, a connective, or a gloss).
resolved_doubts.options: Keep as printed by Vinc. (adopted); possibly delete {μέλος} or obelize.
resolved_doubts.evidence: Vincent has no note, so this is presumably P's text. No other witness has the passage.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 4 : 1: μέλος kept as printed by Vincent; the author uses μέλος of a sung span (27.12 μέλος συναπαρτίζεσθαι). One judge (Claude A, low confidence) would delete it.

resolved_doubts.issue: τὸν προλαμβανόμενον φθόγγον is printed by Vincent without note. The technical name of the first (lowest) note of the Greater Perfect System is προσλαμβανόμενος; as far as I know, προλαμβανόμενος ('taken first') is not a note name.
resolved_doubts.options: Keep προλαμβανόμενον (P as printed by Vinc.), 'the note taken first', i.e. the base term (cf. 29.17 κείσθω πρῶτος ἐν ἀριθμοῖς ὅρος, the number 6); or correct to προσλαμβανόμενον (one letter; conjecture, printed by the arbiter's decision). Decided 30.10.2026 by two judges: P's form is kept (it gives an acceptable sense; inside a P-only passage a conjecture is printed only when the single witness gives none).
resolved_doubts.evidence: Both readings refer to the same note. The section counts the notes of the fifteen-note Greater Perfect System: in Bas. 28.19-22 the 8th is paired with the 1st, the 11th with the 4th, the 12th with the 5th and the 15th with the 8th. The example numbers 6 : 8 : 9 : 12 : 16 : 18 : 24 stand for exactly these notes (1, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 15). P's six ἔμμεσα (fourth, fifth, octave, δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων, δὶς διὰ πέντε, double octave) are the intervals from note 1 to these notes. Note 1 of the system is the proslambanomenos, so the base term 6 is the proslambanomenos, and the two readings are not opposed. The loss of σ, in P or in Vincent's print, would be trivial; Vincent's print divides προ-|λαμβανόμενον at the line end. προσλαμβανόμενον is printed (arbiter's decision): it is the author's own name for note 1 (25.4–5, all witnesses) and the technical term the sense requires. The human editor may prefer P's form, which gives a tolerable sense.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 in the cross-check of the 25 places: προλαμβανόμενον (P) kept, προσλαμβανόμενον in the apparatus (all four judges).

resolved_doubts.issue: In «καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν δὲ οἱ τῶν ἐν μέσῳ» the phrase must denote the composite intervals (ἔμμεσα), as the resumption shows: τοῦ μὲν τῶν ἐμμέσων διαστημάτων λόγου καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν (340.25-26), against κατὰ σειρὰν … τῶν ἀμέσων. Taken by itself, however, 'the intervals in the middle' would rather fit the ἄμεσα, which the same passage describes as μεταξὺ τούτων κείμενα (340.11).
resolved_doubts.options: (a) Keep οἱ τῶν ἐν μέσῳ as printed (adopted), understood as 'those with notes in the middle', a paraphrase of ἔμμεσα. (b) Correct to οἱ τῶν ἐμμέσων (reviewer's conjecture), as at 340.25 and in the opposition ἔμμεσα / ἄμεσα of 340.7-11.
resolved_doubts.evidence: Vincent has no note, so ἐν μέσῳ is presumably P's text as he read it. In Byzantine pronunciation ἐμμέσων and ἐν μέσῳ hardly differ (the nasal assimilated before μ, and ω / ῳ), so a phonetic corruption is easy. The sense is not in doubt: the translator should render it as the composite (ἔμμεσα) intervals.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 4 : 1: ἐμμέσων (conjecture) printed for ἐν μέσῳ (Vinc.); GPT-6.1 Terra keeps ἐν μέσῳ. The passage calls this class ἔμμεσα (340.7) and resumes it as τοῦ μὲν τῶν ἐμμέσων διαστημάτων λόγου καθ’ ὑπερβατόν (340.25-26); 'those ἐν μέσῳ' would naturally be the intervals lying between, i.e. the ἄμεσα (340.11 μεταξὺ τούτων κείμενα). ἔμμεσος/ἄμεσος is the logicians' pair (LSJ, DGE s.v. ἔμμεσος), which fits the comparison with syllogisms. The same confusion is found at Bas. 31.10 (ἐμμέσω H : ἐν μέσῳ Bas. Par. V).

Claude A.form: καθ’ ὑπερβατὸν δέ, οἱ τῶν ἐμμέσων

sections.title_en: The fifth judged by pitch; how the ratios were found; the systems
sections.title_ru: Квинта определяется по высоте; как найдены отношения; системы
sections.greek:
ἐπεί τοί γε τὸ |30.3|διὰ πέντε διάστημα λόγον ἡμιόλιον ἔχον, |30.4|οὐ πρὸς τὴν ὑπεροχὴν τῆς τῶν φθόγγων πο|30.5|σότητος, ἣν ἔχει πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ αὐτοῦ συγ|30.6|κρινόμενος, φαίνεται ἡμιόλιος· πρὸς μὲν |30.7|γὰρ τὸν πρῶτον φθόγγον πενταπλασίων |30.8|εὑρίσκεται, πρὸς δὲ τὸν δεύτερον διπλα|30.9|σιημιόλιος, πρὸς δὲ τὸν τρίτον ἐπιδιμε|30.10|ρής, πρὸς δὲ τὸν τέταρτον ἐπιτέταρτος, |30.11|ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ δὲ δείκνυται ἡμιόλιος. πρὸς |30.12|τὴν ἐπίτασιν τοιγαροῦν τῆς ὀξύτητος, οὐ |30.13|πρὸς τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν φθόγγων, κρίνεται ἡ|30.14|μιόλιος. τὸ δ’ αὐτὸ καὶ περὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς |30.15|τῶν λόγων νοήσομεν. ἐξεύρηνται δὲ οἱ τοι|30.16|οῦτοι τῶν διαστάσεων λόγοι ἀπὸ τῆς διαφο|30.17|ρᾶς τοῦ μήκους τῶν χορδῶν, ἢ τῆς παχύτη|30.18|τος, ἢ τῆς τάσεως γινομένης κατὰ τὴν στρο|30.19|φὴν τῶν κολλάβων, ἢ γνωριμώτερον ἀπὸ τῆς |30.20|ἐξαρτήσεως τῶν βαρῶν· ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἐμ|30.21|πνευστῶν, ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐρύτητος τῶν κοιλι|30.22|ῶν, ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιτάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος |30.23|καὶ ἀνέσεως.

⟨⟨Ἰστέον δὲ ὡς ἐπὶ μὲν τῆς τάσεως ἢ τῆς ἐξαρτήσεως ἡ ἐπὶ πλέον ἐπίτασις καὶ ἡ ἐπὶ μᾶλλον βαρύτης τὴν ἐπὶ ὀξὺ μελῳδίαν ἐργάζεται· ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς παχύτητος τῶν νευρῶν ἢ τοῦ μήκους τούτων ἢ τῶν αὐλῶν ἢ τῆς τῶν τρημάτων διατάσεως τὸ πλεονάζον τούτων τινὸς †ἀμφότερον† τῆς μελῳδίας εἶδος συνίστησι.⟩⟩

Τῶν δὲ συστημάτων τὸ μέν |30.24|ἐστι τετράχορδον, τὰς τοῦ διὰ τεσσάρων |30.25|ἁπάσας ἐμπεριέχον δυνάμεις· τὸ δὲ πεν|31.1|τάχορδον, τὰς τοῦ ⟨διὰ⟩ πέντε δυνάμεις πε|31.2|ριλαμβάνον· τὸ δὲ ὀκτάχορδον, τὴν ὅλην |31.3|τοῦ διὰ πασῶν περιέχον ἰσχύν· τὸ δὲ κατὰ |31.4|συνέχειαν ἑκκαιδεκάχορδον, τὴν τοῦ δὶς |31.5|διὰ πασῶν ὁλοσχερῆ συνέχον διάστασιν, |31.6|διπλᾶς τὰς δυνάμεις ἀποφερόμενον· αὐ|31.7|τάς τε γὰρ τὰς προειρημένας καὶ τὰς τοῦ |31.8|δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων καὶ τοῦ δὶς διὰ πέντε |31.9|καὶ τοῦ δὶς διὰ πασῶν ἐν ἑαυτῷ περιέχει.

departures.source: H Par. (V τοὺς, but om. πρὸ)
departures.reason: Bas. stands alone against H Par. V. The plural is needed: the fifth note is then compared with each of the four notes before it (30.7-11: first, second, third, fourth), not with one.

departures.source: P (Vinc. 342.19–24), with Vincent's correction ἐξαρτήσεως and one crux (†ἀμφότερον†) inside the passage (see apparatus)
departures.reason: A passage found only in P, at this place (Vinc.: it is wholly missing from the edition, which goes straight from ἀνέσεως to τῶν δὲ διαστ.). Printed in ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩ under the edition's rules. Its matter is a summary of Adrastus in Theon of Smyrna p. 65.10-66.11 Hiller (more weight gives the higher note; greater length and thickness of strings, and length and width of the holes of pipes, give the lower), so it is most probably a learned reader's addition, not the author's text. Within it ἐξαρτήσεως is Vinc.'s correction of P's ἐξαντήσεων (the word is in Theon p. 57.4 and 65.13 H.), and ἀμφότερον is obelised (see doubts).

departures.source: P (Vinc. 342.25–26), against Bas. H Par. V
departures.reason: Bas. Par. H V have διαστημάτων; P has συστημάτων, and Vincent already called the edition's reading a 'leçon fautive'. The author's own terminology decides. He defines a system as a compass of intervals and harmonia as the arrangement of systems (24.17–19). The very next sentence, in all witnesses, sets the systems against the intervals within them (Διαφέρει δὲ τὰ συστήματα τῶν ἐν μέσῳ διαστημάτων, 31.10), and he goes on to call the tetrachord and its successors systems (τὰ τοιαῦτα συστήματα, 31.13–14; τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν συστημάτων, 32.21–22, after the genera of the tetrachord; τῶν ἑξῆς συστημάτων, 33.1). The list itself keeps system and interval apart: the tetrachord holds the δυνάμεις of the fourth, the octachord the power of the octave, the sixteen-chord the διάστασις of the double octave. With διαστημάτων the author would call the tetrachord an interval and in the next sentence oppose systems to intervals. The corruption is easy: assimilation to τῶν δὲ διαστημάτων at the head of the paragraph on the intervals (25.19) and to τῶν διαστάσεων (30.16). The agreement of Bas. H Par. V weighs little here, since their common archetype errs two lines below (om. διὰ, 31.1). P's text of this passage is revised elsewhere (30.21–23 and the added paragraph), so συστημάτων may be a learned correction rather than an inherited reading (the reviewer compares Theon of Smyrna p. 49.14–17 Hiller, where tetrachords, pentachords and octachords are called systems); even so it restores the author's usage. Arbiter's decision on the reviewer's proposal; for the human editor's confirmation.
The neuter is required by τὸ … τετράχορδον, as with the parallel participles περιλαμβάνον, περιέχον and συνέχον. Bas. stands alone, probably a misprint (o/ω).

departures.source: Xyl. (margin: «† διὰ πέντε»); conjecture, no witness
departures.reason: The term is always διὰ πέντε: compare τοῦ διὰ τεσσάρων (30.24), τοῦ διὰ πασῶν (31.3), τοῦ δὶς διὰ πέντε (31.8). Bas. Par. H V all lack διὰ, so the omission is archetypal. It is supplied in ⟨ ⟩ because no witness has it.
ὕλην does not construe next to the object ἰσχύν. ὅλην ('the whole power of the octave') matches ἁπάσας (30.25) and ὁλοσχερῆ (31.5). ὕλην is an error shared by Par. and V and carried into Bas.

This is the author's word for an interval or extent (τῶν διαστάσεων λόγοι, 30.16, in all witnesses). H agrees with V, and V is Par.'s closest relative in this section (they share the error ὕλην, 31.2), so διάτασιν looks like an innovation of the printed tradition (Par., followed by Bas.).

apparatus.entry: ἔχον Bas. H Par.] ἔχων V
apparatus.note: o/ω, and possibly only a spelling slip. Taken literally it makes the participle masculine, in line with συγκρινόμενος … ἡμιόλιος later in the same anacoluthic sentence. P not reported here: Vinc.'s fragment 3 begins at 30.15.

apparatus.entry: τοὺς πρὸ H Par.] τὸν πρὸ Bas. | τοὺς V
apparatus.note: V omits πρὸ (πρὸς τοὺς αὐτοῦ). H writes τοὺς in an unusual form (τ-ο-ι-ς with grave), read τοὺς. The plural is required by the four comparisons that follow.

apparatus.entry: ἐξεύρηνται Bas. Par. V] ἐξά̣ρηνται H
apparatus.note: In H (68r.10-11 ἐξά̣ρην|ται) the second vowel is uncertain. As it stands the form is not Greek; it may hide ἐξῄρηνται, ἐξήρτηνται ('depend on', with a lost τ; an option noted by the H transcriber) or a mis-shaped ευ. ἐξεύρηνται ('have been discovered') is supported by the author's source for 30.15-23, Theon of Smyrna p. 56.9-57.6 Hiller (Adrastus): Pythagoras is said to have first found (ἀνευρηκέναι, 56.10) the ratios of the consonances, ἐξετάσας τοὺς λόγους by string length and thickness, peg tension, weights and wind instruments. γνωριμώτερον also suits a verb of discovery. Vinc. prints the edition here, so P is not reported.

apparatus.entry: γινομένης Bas. Par. V] γενομένης H
apparatus.note: H abbreviates γενομ(ένης). The author's source decides for the present: Theon Sm. p. 57.2-3 H. τῆς τάσεως γινομένης κατὰ τὴν στροφὴν τῶν κολλάβων. Vinc.'s first paragraph, said to be printed from the edition, has γενομένης without a footnote, although Par. has γινομένης; whether this silently reports P cannot be told, so it is not counted as evidence for P.

apparatus.entry: ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐρύτητος τῶν κοιλιῶν Bas. H Par. V] ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν αὐλῶν ἢ τῶν τρημάτων ἀφορότητος P
apparatus.note: From Vinc. 342 n. 5, which prints αὐλῶι, evidently for αὐλῶν. ἀφορότης has no entry in LSJ; Vinc. glosses it 'délimitation' and calls it new. The main tradition's wording is the author's: it reproduces Theon Sm. p. 57.4-5 H. (ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἐμπνευστῶν καὶ διὰ τῆς εὐρύτητος τῶν κοιλιῶν). P's clause is a later rewording, in step with its added paragraph on pipes and holes, whose matter goes back to Theon p. 66.6-9 H. (τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὴν εὐρύτητα τῶν τρημάτων). P's ἀφορότητος may itself hide εὐρύτητος (a suggestion only, not used).

apparatus.entry: ἐπιτάσεως Bas. H Par. V] τάσεως P
apparatus.note: From Vinc. 342 n. 5, printed ἢ ἀπὸ τῆ τάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος (τῆ for τῆς). Theon Sm. p. 57.6 H. (διὰ τῆς ἐπιτάσεως καὶ ἀνέσεως τοῦ πνεύματος) confirms the main tradition.

apparatus.entry: καὶ ἀνέσεως Bas. H Par. V] om. P
apparatus.note: From Vinc. 342 n. 5: P's clause ends at τοῦ πνεύματος. Theon Sm. p. 57.6 H. has καὶ ἀνέσεως.

apparatus.entry: ⟨⟨Ἰστέον δὲ … εἶδος συνίστησι⟩⟩ P (Vinc. 342.19–24)] om. Bas. H Par. V
apparatus.note: Vinc. 342.19-24, from P fol. 4r, said to be wholly absent from the edition. In P it follows P's own shorter clause ending …τάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος. Here it is printed after the main tradition's ἀνέσεως. Its content summarises Theon Sm. p. 65.10-66.11 H.

apparatus.entry: ἐξαρτήσεως Vinc.] ἐξαντήσεων P
apparatus.note: Vinc. 342 n. 6 ('Ms. ἐξαντήσεων'). The correction is certain: compare ἀπὸ τῆς ἐξαρτήσεως τῶν βαρῶν, Bas. 30.19-20, and the pairing with τάσεως. The word is not new, as Vinc. thought: Theon Sm. p. 57.4 H. (κατὰ τὴν ἐξάρτησιν τῶν βαρῶν) and p. 65.12-13 H. (ἐπὶ τῆς τάσεως τῆς γινομένης διὰ τῆς ἐξαρτήσεως τῶν βαρῶν), the latter in the very argument that P's paragraph summarises.

apparatus.entry: ἐργάζεται P] ἐξάγεται Vinc. in nota (dub.)
apparatus.note: Vinc. 342 n. 7, 'Peut-être ἐξάγεται'. P's ἐργάζεται makes good sense ('produces the melody towards the high'; compare Theon Sm. p. 65.14-16 H., where the greater weight τὸν ὀξύτερον ποιήσει φθόγγον) and is kept.

apparatus.entry: †ἀμφότερον† P (Vinc., no footnote) | θάτερον, βαρύτερον, ἀμβλύτερον coni.
apparatus.note: Gives no sense where the argument needs 'the opposite (low) kind of melody'. Theon Sm. p. 65.10-66.11 H., the source of the paragraph's content, makes greater length and thickness of strings, and greater length and width of the holes of wind instruments, produce the lower notes. See doubts. Judged 4 : 1 to keep the obeli (30.10.2026).

apparatus.entry: συστημάτων P] διαστημάτων Bas. H Par. V
apparatus.note: Vinc. 342.25-26 prints Τῶν δὲ συστημάτων and calls the edition's διαστημάτων a 'leçon fautive'. Adopted from P against Bas. H Par. V on the author's own usage (24.17–19, 31.10, 31.13–14, 32.21–22, 33.1): see departures; the argument is recorded in the doubts.

apparatus.entry: ἐμπεριέχον H Par. V] ἐμπεριέχων Bas.
apparatus.note: The neuter agrees with τὸ … τετράχορδον. Bas. stands alone, probably a misprint (o/ω). P not reported from here on: Vinc. stops at τετράχορδον, κ. τ. λ.

apparatus.entry: τοῦ ⟨διὰ⟩ πέντε Xyl.] τοῦ πέντε Bas. H Par. V
apparatus.note: Xylander's marginal note «† διὰ πέντε», keyed to † in the text. No witness has διὰ.

apparatus.entry: ὅλην H Xyl.] ὕλην Bas. Par. V
apparatus.note: Xylander's marginal conjecture «* ὅλην» is confirmed by H.

apparatus.entry: διάστασιν H V] διάτασιν Bas. Par.
apparatus.note: V writes στ with a ligature, fairly clear. Compare the author's τῶν διαστάσεων λόγοι, 30.16.

orthographica.Bas: 30.2 ἐπείτοιγε printed as one word; normalised to ἐπεί τοί γε (enclitic before enclitic). 30.10 ἐπιδιμερὴς· and 31.3 ἰσχὺν. carry a grave before punctuation. 30.11 δείκνηται is a misprint (η for υ) for δείκνυται (H Par. V), corrected as a spelling-level slip; it is not a variant. 30.19 κολάβων has a single λ, as in H Par. V; normalised to κολλάβων, the standard spelling (κόλλαβος, LSJ; so Theon Sm. p. 57.3 H., the source of this passage, and Vinc.), since a simplified double consonant is spelling, not morphology (cf. ἄρρευστον in P fr. 1, section 3; ὀξέος for the unanimous ὀξέως, 28.18). 30.25 ἐμπεριέχων (o/ω) goes in the apparatus because it changes the gender. Xylander's reference signs † (31.1) and * (31.2) are not reproduced. Ligatures and compendia are expanded (ἐξεύρηνται, μέν ἐστι, πέντε, περιλαμβάνον, ὁλοσχερῆ, ἑαυτῷ). 30.17 παχύτη- ends its line without a hyphen. Punctuation is redone for sense: the full stop after ἡμιόλιος (30.6) becomes a raised point; the ratio series takes commas; the comma after συνέχειαν (31.4) is dropped.
orthographica.H: 30.2 ἐπεί τοι γε. 31.5 and 31.9 διαπασῶν written as one word (δι|απασῶν, διαπασῶν). 31.4 ἐκκαιδεκάχορδον with smooth breathing. 31.9 iota adscript in ἑαυτῶι. 30.19 κολάβων. Abbreviations: τ(ῆς) 30.4, τ(οὺς) 30.14, χορδῶ(ν) 30.17, γενομ(ένης) 30.18, πν(εύματο)ς 30.22, τ(ὰς) 31.7. 30.5 τοὺς is written τ-ο-ι-ς with grave. Red line-initials inside a sentence: Γὰρ (68r.2) and Τῆς (68r.17); these are rubrication, not text division. Acute before punctuation (ἐπιδιμερής, ἰσχύν). High and low points often fall at different clause boundaries from Bas. (διάστημα· λόγον; ἔχον. οὐ; τάσεως· γενομ(ένης); κατὰ συνέχειαν ἐκκαιδεκάχορδον. τὴν). The line ends at ἐμπεριέ|χον, πενταπλασί|ων and similar places. The provisional readings in Claude's H notes (68r.7 τοιιδροῶν, 68r.10 μονήσομεν, 68v.2 ἰαχώ) are superseded by the decided transcription (τοιγαροῦν, νοήσομεν, ἰσχύν): no variants.
orthographica.Par: 30.2 ἐπείτοιγε as one word, as in Bas. 30.19 κολάβων. Acute before punctuation (ἐπιδιμερής, ἰσχύν). Its own punctuation: φθόγγων, ποσότητος (25r.5); ἐπίτασιν, τοιγαροῦν (25r.14); no comma after συγκρινόμενος; raised points in the τετράχορδον series. Otherwise Par. is orthographically identical to Bas. in this section, and correctly reads δείκνυται and ἐμπεριέχον.
orthographica.V: 30.2 ἐπείτοι γε. 30.20 πὶ for ἐπὶ: a new period begins after βαρῶν: and the red initial ε meant for the margin was never executed (margin blank), so this is not a variant. 30.23 μὲν with grave before the enclitic ἐστι. 30.19 κολάβων. π(νεύματο)ς abbreviated (30.22). Rubricated letters: π of πεντα|πλασίων (80r.15), Τὸ (80v.2), ἐν (81r.6). Comma in τὸ δ’ αὐτὸ, καὶ (80v.2). 30.5 τοὺς is written in the hand's -ους form that resembles -οις. 30.3 ἔχων (o/ω) goes in the apparatus because it changes the gender.
orthographica.P: Known only from Vinc. 342. His first paragraph (342.13-18) is printed from the edition. There he prints κολλάβων with n. 4 'Éd. κολάβων', so P may spell it with λλ. In n. 5 the printed αὐλῶι and τῆ are evidently slips or unexpanded abbreviations for αὐλῶν, τῆς; ἐ. is most likely Vinc.'s own shortening of ἐμπνευστῶν, already printed in his text (compare his ἀ. τ. φ. ἢ τ. χ., 342.7, and διαστ., συστ., 342.12), not necessarily a compendium of P. Vinc.'s γενομένης (30.18) has no footnote and is not counted as P's. Vinc. capitalises paragraph openings (Ἐξεύρηνται, Ἰστέον, Τῶν); this text begins new paragraphs at Ἰστέον and Τῶν δὲ συστημάτων, not at ἐξεύρηνται.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: τῶν δὲ συστημάτων ('of the systems, one is the tetrachord…')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: τῶν δὲ διαστημάτων ('of the intervals, one is the tetrachord…')
alternatives_for_translation.why: The reading of all four main witnesses, and so of every translation made from the printed editions. συστημάτων (P) is printed because it is the author's own terminology and leads into the next sentence (Διαφέρει δὲ τὰ συστήματα τῶν ἐν μέσῳ διαστημάτων, 31.10); the translator should footnote the variant.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: διάστασιν
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: διάτασιν ('the whole stretch/extension of the double octave')
alternatives_for_translation.why: It also makes sense and was the text of the printed tradition, and hence of the older Latin versions.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: γινομένης
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: γενομένης ('the tension brought about by turning the pegs')
alternatives_for_translation.why: This is the oldest witness's reading and is good Greek; the difference is one of aspect only. The author's source (Theon Sm. p. 57.3 H.) has γινομένης, so H's aorist is secondary; listed for completeness only.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἐμπνευστῶν, ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐρύτητος τῶν κοιλιῶν, ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιτάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἀνέσεως
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἐμπνευστῶν, ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν αὐλῶν ἢ τῶν τρημάτων ἀφορότητος, ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς τάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος ('in wind instruments, from the ἀφορότης [spacing? delimitation?] of the pipes or holes, or from the tension of the breath')
alternatives_for_translation.why: This is P's reworded clause, which its added paragraph (on pipes and holes) presupposes. It is useful for a note on the P passage printed in ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩. The adopted wording is the author's: it follows Theon Sm. p. 57.4-6 H.

sections.p_treatment: P fragment 3 (Vinc. 342.8-26). Lines 342.1-7 are the end of fragment 2 and belong to the previous section. Vinc. places the fragment at the 6th line from the bottom of Par. 25r, i.e. Par. 25r.17, which is Bas. 30.15 ἐξεύρηνται. His first paragraph (342.13-18) is printed from the edition and is not used as evidence for P, except where his footnotes report P. n. 4 ('Éd. κολάβων'; Vinc. κολλάβων) is orthographic and goes in orthographica. n. 5 gives P's different wording of the wind-instrument clause and yields three apparatus entries at Bas. 30.21-23; the main tradition's wording there is confirmed as the author's by his source, Theon of Smyrna p. 57.4-6 Hiller, so P's clause is a later revision. Vinc.'s γενομένης at 30.18 has no footnote and is not ascribed to P. P is cited as not reported elsewhere in 30.15-20. The second paragraph (342.19-24, Ἰστέον … συνίστησι) is in P only; its content summarises Theon p. 65.10-66.11 H. It is printed in ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩ immediately after ἀνέσεως (Bas. 30.23), from Vinc.'s text, with three decisions: ἐξαρτήσεως adopted from Vinc.'s correction of P's ἐξαντήσεων (n. 6; the word is in Theon); P's ἐργάζεται kept against Vinc.'s tentative ἐξάγεται (n. 7); ἀμφότερον obelised. P's variants in the preceding clause do not alter the main text. In P that clause ends …ἀπὸ τῆς τάσεως τοῦ πνεύματος; here the paragraph follows the main tradition's …καὶ ἀνέσεως. P's Τῶν δὲ συστημάτων (342.25-26) is recorded as a variant of διαστημάτων at 30.23 and not adopted; it is listed among the doubts and the alternatives, and the reviewer disputes the choice. After τετράχορδον Vinc. gives only κ. τ. λ., so P is not reported for the rest of the section.

resolved_doubts.issue: Decided by the arbiter: τῶν δὲ συστημάτων (P) is printed against τῶν δὲ διαστημάτων (Bas. Par. H V); see departures. Kept here as a record, because the text follows P against all four main witnesses. The tetrachord, pentachord, octachord and sixteen-chord are, in strict theory and in the author's own definitions, systems, not intervals.
resolved_doubts.options: (a) διαστημάτων (Bas. Par. H V; the editor's choice); (b) συστημάτων (P; the reviewer's proposal, printed).
resolved_doubts.evidence: For (b): Theon of Smyrna p. 49.14-17 Hiller (Adrastus) calls exactly the tetrachord, pentachord and octachord τὰ λεγόμενα συστήματα, made up of διαστήματα; the author demonstrably uses Theon in this section (30.15-23 follows Theon p. 56.9-57.6 H. almost word for word; ὁλοσχερῆ, 31.5, echoes Theon 49.15). Cleonides, Isag. 1 defines a σύστημα as made up of more than one interval, and Vinc. calls διαστημάτων a 'leçon fautive'. The next section begins διαφέρει δὲ τὰ συστήματα τῶν … (H 68v.9; V 81r.6), which follows naturally on a list of systems. The archetype of H Par. V is demonstrably faulty two lines later (om. διὰ, 31.1). For (a): the agreement of the oldest witness H with Par. and V, that is, of both branches. The author uses his terms loosely (the δὶς διὰ πασῶν is called a διάστασις at 31.5), and he may well call these 'intervals' and then distinguish system from interval in the next sentence. P's text of this whole passage is revised: its wind-instrument clause departs from Theon where H Par. V follow him, and it adds a paragraph drawn from Theon p. 65-66. So συστημάτων may be a learned correction by a reader who knew the definition, perhaps from the same Theon. Arbiter's decision for (b): the author's own usage is decisive (24.17–19, definitions of system and harmonia; τὰ τοιαῦτα συστήματα, 31.13–14; τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν συστημάτων, 32.21–22; τῶν ἑξῆς συστημάτων, 33.1), and a 'more difficult' reading that contradicts the next sentence is not to be preferred. For the human editor's confirmation.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 5 : 0: συστημάτων (P) kept, as printed.

Claude A.form: τῶν δὲ συστημάτων, τὸ μέν ἐστι τετράχορδον

resolved_doubts.issue: In P's added paragraph, τὸ πλεονάζον τούτων τινὸς ἀμφότερον τῆς μελῳδίας εἶδος συνίστησι gives no sense. The argument needs 'the opposite (low) kind of melody', in contrast to τὴν ἐπὶ ὀξὺ μελῳδίαν of the first member: more thickness or length of string or pipe, or more distance of the holes, lowers the pitch.
resolved_doubts.options: Print †ἀμφότερον† (done). My own conjectures, none supported by a checked parallel: θάτερον ('the other kind', i.e. the low); βαρύτερον; ἀμβλύτερον (graphically closest to ἀμφότερον). A lacuna is a weaker possibility (τὸ πλεονάζον ⟨καὶ τὸ ἐλλεῖπον⟩ … ἀμφότερον, 'excess and deficiency produce both kinds'), but it does not fit the antithesis with the first member. It may also be a slip in Vinc.'s transcription, which cannot be checked.
resolved_doubts.evidence: Vinc. prints ἀμφότερον without a footnote. The sense required is confirmed by the source of the paragraph's content, Theon of Smyrna p. 65.10-66.11 Hiller (Adrastus): more weight gives the higher note, while length and thickness of strings, and length and width of the holes of wind instruments, give the lower (οἱ βαρύτεροι, 66.7). The parallel decides the sense but not the word, so the word that is needed cannot be recovered with confidence.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 4 : 1: †ἀμφότερον† kept. The sense 'the other (low) kind' is certain, but no conjecture is at once idiomatic and close to the letters; θάτερον (Claude B), βαρύτερον and ἀμβλύτερον go to the apparatus.

Claude A.form: τὸ πλεονάζον τούτων τινὸς †ἀμφότερον† τῆς μελῳδίας εἶδος συνίστησι.

GPT-6.1 Sol.form: τὸ πλεονάζον τούτων τινὸς †ἀμφότερον† τῆς μελῳδίας εἶδος συνίστησι

resolved_doubts.issue: Number check on ἑκκαιδεκάχορδον. The double octave spans fifteen notes (2 × 8 − 1); the usual term for a fifteen-note system is πεντεκαιδεκάχορδον (LSJ s.v. cites Adrastus in Theon of Smyrna p. 64 H. and Ptolemy, Harmonics 3.1).
resolved_doubts.options: Keep ἑκκαιδεκάχορδον, the reading of all witnesses (adopted). Emendation to πεντεκαιδεκάχορδον is not justified.
resolved_doubts.evidence: The author builds the system κατὰ συνέχειαν as two octachords in a row (8+8) and stresses doubling (διπλᾶς τὰς δυνάμεις …). The 16 is his own count, not a scribal error: at 25.11–12 (all witnesses) he speaks of τὸ ἐν πεντεκαιδεκαχόρδῳ ἑκκαιδεκάχορδον, the sixteen-chord, built of two octachords κατὰ συνέχειαν, realised on fifteen notes; a numeral confusion ιε΄/ις΄ in an exemplar would be a possible mechanism, but no witness supports it. The translator may want a note. Other numbers in the section were checked and agree in all witnesses: the fifth note against the first is 5:1 (πενταπλασίων), against the second 5:2 (διπλασιημιόλιος; the term for 5:2 is in Theon Sm. p. 110 H.), against the third 5:3 (ἐπιδιμερής), against the fourth 5:4 (ἐπιτέταρτος), and none of these is 3:2 (ἡμιόλιος), as the text says. The doubled consonances in 31.7-9 (double fourth, double fifth, double octave) are the doubling of the three named before. As at 28.6–12 and 29.8–15, δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων and δὶς διὰ πέντε are the author's names for the fourth and the fifth above the octave (8:3, 3:1), and the translator should render them as there.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Decided 30.10.2026 by five independent judges (Claude Opus 5.5 ×2, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol; Codex ultra with web search for the GPT judges), each deciding from the witnesses after reference research in lexica, grammars, the theorists and handbooks; options anonymised and shuffled, 5 : 0: ἑκκαιδεκάχορδον, the reading of all witnesses, kept as the author's own count.

sections.title_en: Systems and intervals; the three genera of the fourth
sections.title_ru: Системы и интервалы; три рода кварты
sections.greek: |31.10|Διαφέρει δὲ τὰ συστήματα τῶν ἐν μέσῳ δια|31.11|στημάτων, τῷ τὰ μὲν ἐν ὕλῃ τὴν σύστασιν |31.12|ἔχειν, τὰ δὲ διαστήματα ἐξ ἀφαιρέσεως |31.13|τῆς ὕλης νοεῖσθαι. τῆς δὲ ἁρμονίας ἴδιον τὸ |31.14|τὰ τοιαῦτα συστήματα συντάττειν καὶ συ|31.15|ναρμολογεῖν πρὸς τὸ τοιόνδε τῆς μελῳδίας |31.16|γένος, οἷον τὸ διάτονον, τὸ χρωματικὸν |31.17|καὶ τὸ παρωνύμως ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ἁρμονίας ἁρ|31.18|μονικὸν προσαγορευόμενον. εἰ μὲν οὖν |31.19|διὰ τόνων τὸ πλεῖστον ἡ ἁρμονία προάγοι|31.20|το, τὸ διάτονον οὕτω καλούμενον κατα|31.21|σκευάζεται γένος· εἰ δὲ δι’ ἡμιτονίων, |31.22|τὸ χρωματικόν· εἰ δὲ διέσεσι μᾶλλον |31.23|ἡ ἁρμονία συνέχεται, τὸ ἁρμονικὸν λε|31.24|γόμενον ἀπαρτίζεται μέλος. οὐ μὴν τὸ |31.25|πᾶν διὰ τόνων τὰ τῆς ἁρμονίας προφέ|32.1|ρεται, οὐδὲ δι’ ἡμιτονίων τὸ πᾶν, οὐδὲ τὸ |32.2|πᾶν ἐκ διέσεων· οὐδὲ γὰρ δυνατόν. ἀλλ’ |32.3|ἐπεὶ τρισὶ διαστάσεσι τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων ἀ|32.4|πήρτισται, δυσὶ δὲ τόνοις καὶ ἡμιτονίῳ διεί|32.5|ληπται, δύο τονιαίων διαστημάτων ἐντιθε|32.6|μένων ἀνάγκη τὸ λοιπὸν τελεῖν ἡμιτόνιον. |32.7|καὶ τοῦτ’ ἂν εἴη τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων διάτονον |32.8|ὀνομαζόμενον γένος, ἐξ ἡμιτονίου καὶ δύο |32.9|ἀπαρτιζόμενον τόνων. εἰ δὲ δύο εἴη τὰ ἡμι|32.10|τόνια, τὸ λοιπὸν γένοιτ’ ἂν ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρ|32.11|σεως διάστημα, τριημιτόνιον ἀσύνθετον· ἐξ |32.12|ἡμιτονίων δύο καὶ τριημιτονίου συγκεκρα|32.13|μένον. εἴη δ’ ἂν τοῦτο τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων γένος |32.14|χρωματικόν, παθητικώτερόν τε τοῦ προτέ|32.15|ρου καὶ γοερώτερον. εἰ δὲ κατὰ δύο διέσεις |32.16|ἡ μελῳδία προάγοιτο, θάτερον ἔσται τῶν δια|32.17|στημάτων ἓν διτόνιον ἐκ συμφθάρσεως· καὶ |32.18|τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων τοῦτο γένος ἁρμονικὸν ὀνο|32.19|μάζεται, τῷ εἶναι ἄριστον, ἐκ τῆς κοινῆς ἁρμο|32.20|νίας τὴν παρωνυμίαν ἀπενεγκάμενον.

departures.reason: The subject of συνέχεται needs the article, as in the parallel clauses ἡ ἁρμονία προάγοιτο (31.19) and ἡ μελῳδία προάγοιτο (32.16). The disjunctive ἢ was suggested by the preceding μᾶλλον (μᾶλλον ἢ, 'rather than'). It leaves a comparison without a second member and makes ἁρμονία an anarthrous subject. Bas. Par. share ἢ. For V's reading see the doubts.

Bas. stands alone against all the other witnesses. Bas. took the text over from the earlier edition, as Par. shows, and Par. has ἐν-, so ἐκ- is a misprint of Bas. or an unsupported change by Xylander. ἐντίθημι, 'insert, place within', describes the two tone-intervals placed inside the fourth exactly: once they are in, the remainder must be a semitone.

γοέτερον is not a Greek form. The comparative of γοερός (short syllable before the ending) is regularly γοερώτερος, like σοφώτερος. LSJ s.v. γοερός gives no comparative (checked), so the form is a regular formation, not a recorded rarity. The syllable -ρω- was lost, perhaps under the influence of the familiar ending -έτερος (ἡμέτερος, ἑκάτερος). Par. and V share the error, so it is not a misprint of Bas. but an error of the branch the printed text comes from. The oldest witness keeps the correct form.

apparatus.entry: ἡ H Xyl.] ἢ Bas. Par. V
apparatus.note: Xyl. in margin «* ἡ», keyed by the asterisk in the text. Resolved: V reads ἢ, as Bas. and Par. (collation dispute decided against the scan by both checkers); the collator's «ἡ» was a misreading. The entry stands as printed.

apparatus.entry: οὐδὲ Bas. Par. V] οὐ γὰρ H
apparatus.note: H writes γ with the γάρ abbreviation. The series οὐ μὴν … οὐδὲ … οὐδὲ (31.24–32.2) has three parallel members, and a causal γάρ in the second member makes no sense. This is probably an anticipation of οὐδὲ γὰρ δυνατόν two lines below, or a confusion of the δέ and γάρ compendia.

apparatus.entry: διείληπται Bas. H Par.] διείρηπται V
apparatus.note: V's form does not exist. It is either a λ/ρ slip for διείληπται or a blend of διείληπται with διῄρηται (perfect of διαιρέω), which would be pronounced and often written διείρηται. On either explanation the sense is 'is divided into two tones and a semitone'. For διαλαμβάνω 'divide' see LSJ s.v. III (checked by editor and reviewer; no musical sense is given). The ρ was marked uncertain in the collator's first reading ('a descender like ρ'); the established V line reads ρ. Kept in the apparatus at the editor's request; see alternatives for translation.

apparatus.entry: ἐντιθεμένων H Par. V] ἐκτιθεμένων Bas.
apparatus.note: Bas. alone. In Par. the ἐν- is written ἐ with the ν-compendium and is clear at enlargement; V reads ἐν clearly.

apparatus.entry: γοερώτερον H] γοέτερον Bas. Par. V
apparatus.note: H abbreviates γοερώτερο(ν). The shared error of Par. V Bas. links V to the printed tradition. This section varies in substance at five places. Par. V Bas. agree against H at three of them: 31.23 (if V's ἢ stands), 32.1 and 32.15. V stands alone at 32.4–5 (διείρηπται), and Bas. alone at 32.5–6 (ἐκτιθεμένων).

orthographica.Bas: Diplomatic accents and misprints, all normalised silently: τοῖόνδε (31.15, circumflex plus enclitic acute) for τοιόνδε; μαλλον without circumflex (31.22); ἁρμόνικον (31.23, acute misplaced) for ἁρμονικὸν; Αλλ’ without breathing (32.2); δυνατὸν. and χρωματικὸν, with grave before a stop or comma (31.16, 32.2, 32.14), whereas 31.22 has χρωματικόν· with acute; συμφθαρ́- with the acute over the α/ρ junction (32.10); διατεσσάρων set solid without accent (32.18; elsewhere διὰ τεσσάρων). Capitals at sentence openings in mid-line: Τῆς (31.13), Εἰ (31.18), Αλλ’ (32.2). Xylander's reference sign * stands before ἢ at 31.23; the substantive correction is in the apparatus. Compendia, expanded in the transcription: τῷ, τῆς, -ος of γένος/μέλος, δὲ, ἓν, τοῦτο, εἶναι. Punctuation: commas and full stops partly against the sense, e.g. a comma after ἴδιον (31.13), no stop between ἀσύνθετον and ἐξ (32.11), a comma after προτέρου (32.15) and after γένος (32.18).
orthographica.Par: Misprints: παρωνύμας (26r.5) for παρωνύμως, an ω/α slip giving no Greek word that fits the construction, so not recorded in the apparatus (the machine's 'check' is decided as orthographic); λοιπὼν (26r.22) for λοιπὸν; doubled comma «μᾶλλον,,» (26r.12). Correct accents where Bas. errs: τοιόνδε, μᾶλλον, ἁρμονικὸν, δυνατόν, Ἀλλ’. Word division διὰ τεσσάρων at 26v.14–15 (Bas. 32.18 διατεσσάρων). Punctuation differs freely from Bas.: «μέν,» (25v.20); commas after συναρμολογεῖν (26r.3), διαστάσεσι (26r.18), ἀσύνθετον (26v.6–7) and δύο (26v.7); full stops for commas or high points at 26r.4–5, 26r.16, 26r.20, 26v.6, 26v.10, 26v.16; a comma after τοῦτο at 26v.8–9 (εἴη δ’ ἂν τοῦτο, τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων…); a comma after ἄριστον at 26v.16.
orthographica.H: Iota subscript is not written: μέσω, τῶ (τῷ, 68v.10 and 69v.2), ὕλη, ἡμιτονίω, μελωδίας/μελωδία. ἐμ̣μέσω (68v.10) is written as one word with assimilated ν for ἐν μέσῳ. The breathing is missing in αφαιρέσεως (68v.12). τοιόνδε has the correct accent (68v.15). Abbreviations: τῶ(ν), (καὶ), γ(ὰρ), διαστημάτ(ων), γοερώτερο(ν), τ(ὴν). Red initials Δ (68v.19) and Ε (69r.20) begin lines. The Δ stands inside the sentence (εἰ μὲν οὖν | Διὰ τόνων): by the usual Byzantine practice, the enlarged initial of the first full line marks a paragraph that begins in the line before (εἰ μὲν οὖν, 68v.18). The Ε coincides with the sentence Εἰ δὲ κατὰ δύο διέσεις. διὰ τεσσάρων is written as two words, at 69r.22–69v.1 across the line end. Punctuation marks cola with the high point and the low/middle point, often where modern punctuation has none: ἴδιον. τὸ; οἷον. τὸ διάτονον.; τοῦτο. τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων; ἄριστον. ἐκ.
orthographica.V: Iota subscript is written regularly (μέσῳ, τῷ, ὕλῃ, μελῳδίας, ἡμιτονίῳ). Red initials: the κ of καὶ at 81r.15 and 81v.12, the ο of οὐ at 81v.3, the ε of εἴη at 81v.20, and the ἐ of ἐν at 81r.6, which belongs to the preceding section. The dicolon «:» serves as a strong stop (81r.21, 81v.15, 81v.19, 82r.6, 82r.8). διὰ τεσσάρων is written as two words, including at 82r.5 (Bas. 32.18 διατεσσάρων). High points after διαστημάτων (81r.7), ἔχειν (81r.8) and ἀσύνθετον (81v.18); a dicolon after συγκεκραμένον (81v.19). Commas: οἷον, (81r.14); τοῦτο, (81v.20).","P":"Not extant in this section: none of Vincent's three P passages falls within Bas. 31.10–32.20.

doubts.issue: How to construe and punctuate ἐξ ἡμιτονίων δύο καὶ τριημιτονίου συγκεκραμένον. The participle cannot qualify τριημιτόνιον, which cannot be made of itself plus two semitones. It must describe the whole fourth or genus: two semitones plus a trihemitone, 0.5 + 0.5 + 1.5 = 2.5 tones.
doubts.options: (a) As printed in this text: a high point after ἀσύνθετον (with H and V) and a full stop after συγκεκραμένον. The participle is loosely appended and agrees ad sensum with the fourth (τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων), the subject of the whole discussion, parallel to ἐξ ἡμιτονίου καὶ δύο ἀπαρτιζόμενον τόνων of the diatonic (32.8–9). (b) A stop after ἀσύνθετον only: 'compounded of two semitones and a trihemitone, this would be the chromatic genus of the fourth'.
doubts.evidence: All four witnesses put a stop after συγκεκραμένον: Bas. and Par. a full stop, V a dicolon, H a high point. This supports (a). After ἀσύνθετον, H and V have a high point and Par. a comma, so they set the phrase off on both sides; Bas. has no punctuation there. Option (b) would also postpone δ’ behind a six-word phrase. Text keeps (a). The high point after ἀσύνθετον (the reviewer's proposal, adopted by the arbiter in place of the editor's comma) marks the change of reference from the trihemitone back to the fourth. The translator should supply 'the fourth being thus compounded…'.

|32.21|τὸν ὅμοιον δὲ τρόπον καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν συ|32.22|στημάτων ἡ ἁρμονία συντάττει. τῷ γὰρ ἑ|32.23|νὸς τοῦ τετραχόρδου περὶ τὰ διαστήματα |32.24|τοῦ διὰ τεσσάρων συντακτικῷ ὑποδείγμα|32.25|τι, ῥᾴδιον τῷ φιλομαθεῖ καὶ περὶ τῶν ἑξῆς |33.1|συστημάτων καταστοχάζεσθαι. δυσμελῳδι|33.2|κώτατον μέντοι τὸ ἁρμονικὸν γένος τῆς με|33.3|λῳδίας ἐστί, καὶ πολλῆς τριβῆς καὶ συνηθεί|33.4|ας δεόμενον, ὅθεν οὐδ’ εἰς χρῆσιν ῥᾳδίως ἔρ|33.5|χεται. τὸ δὲ διάτονον ἁπλοῦν τε καὶ γεν|33.6|ναῖον καὶ φυσικώτερον· διὸ δὴ τοῦτο παρα|33.7|λαμβάνει καὶ Πλάτων. τούτων δὲ πάλιν |33.8|ἕκαστον ποικίλλεται καὶ εἰς πολλὰς διαιρέ|33.9|σεις καὶ διαφορὰς καὶ εἴδη μελῳδιῶν κα|33.10|τατέμνεται· καὶ νῦν μὲν λύδιον, νῦν δὲ |33.11|φρύγιον, νῦν δὲ δώριον ἐναρμόζεται μέλος, |33.12|ὧν ἐφ’ ἑκάστῳ παιήων, ὑμέναιος, ἐξόδιος |33.13|καὶ ὅσα εἴδη μελῳδιῶν ἀναφαίνεται. οὐ |33.14|γὰρ τῇ τῶν διαστημάτων μόνῃ μεταφορᾷ, οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ |33.15|καὶ ταῖς σχολαιοτέραις καὶ ταχιναῖς μετα|33.16|βάσεσι, διαμοναῖς τε καὶ ῥοαῖς, καὶ ταῖς τῶν |33.17|ἐπαφῶν καὶ κρουμάτων ποικίλαις μεταχει|33.18|ρίσεσι, τὰ μυρία τῶν μελῳδιῶν καὶ |33.19|ποικίλα κατασκευά|33.20|ζεται.

|33.21|Τέλος τῆς μουσικῆς.

departures.source: H (69v.5 τοῦ τε|τραχόρδου); also Xyl.'s margin «* τοῦ»
departures.reason: τὸ cannot be construed. The phrase τῷ … ἑνὸς τοῦ τετραχόρδου … συντακτικῷ ὑποδείγματι needs the genitive article with τετραχόρδου, depending on ὑποδείγματι. Bas. Par. V share the error, which is probably a misread abbreviation of τοῦ. H and Xylander's correction agree.
A Bas. misprint: the ερ-ligature was set for εν. The name of the wedding song (ὑμέναιος) is needed in the list παιήων, ὑμέναιος, ἐξόδιος. Bas. stands alone.

departures.adopted: μόνῃ μεταφορᾷ, οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ
departures.reason: Bas. stands alone against all three witnesses, including Par., the reprint of the editio princeps. Bas. depends on the printed tradition: it shares χολαιοτέραις (33.15) with Par. against H V, and τὸ (32.23) with Par. V against H. So the loss happened in Bas. itself. A skip from μόνῃ to μόνῃ would leave τούτων in place (μόνῃ τούτων διαφορᾷ), so that explanation needs a second loss. There is a one-step explanation in Par.'s layout: 27r.18 … μόνῃ με-| 27r.19 ταφορᾷ. οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων δια-| 27r.20 φορᾷ. ἀλλὰ. Here the words missing in Bas. are exactly those between the line-end syllable με- and the line-end syllable δια- directly below it. A compositor setting from a copy with this lineation could pass from one to the other and produce μόνῃ διαφορᾷ. It is not known whether the 1532 princeps had Par.'s lineation, and a deliberate shortening cannot be ruled out. The fuller text is the better sense. The two negative clauses match the two things just discussed. The shifting (μεταφορά) of the intervals gives the λύδιον/φρύγιον/δώριον melodies. The difference (διαφορά) of the intervals gives the genera, such as the enharmonic and the diatonic just discussed. ἀλλὰ καὶ then adds tempo, sustained notes, flow and instrumental technique.

χολαιοτέραις is not a word. σχολαιότερος ('slower, more leisurely') is the necessary partner of ταχιναῖς ('quick') with μεταβάσεσι. Bas. and Par. share the loss of σ (or the σχ-ligature was misread; see doubts).

apparatus.entry: δὲ Bas. Par. V] γὰρ H
apparatus.note: H writes γ(ὰρ) by abbreviation. It is probably an anticipation of the γὰρ in the next sentence (Bas. 32.22, τῷ γὰρ ἑνὸς). Two explanatory γὰρ-sentences in a row would be awkward, and the first sentence does not explain what precedes it: it is a transition ('in the same way …'). Kept δὲ with Bas. Par. V, against the oldest witness alone.

apparatus.entry: τοῦ H Xyl.] τὸ Bas. Par. V
apparatus.note: Xylander marks τὸ with * and prints «* τοῦ» in the outer margin. It is noteworthy that Par. and V share the error τὸ with Bas.

apparatus.entry: νῦν δὲ φρύγιον Bas. H Par.] νῦν δὲ φρύγιον νῦν δὲ φρύγιον V
apparatus.note: V 82v.5–6: νῦν δὲ, φρύγιον· νῦν δὲ φρύ-|γιον· νῦν δὲ δώριον. This is a simple dittography. The mode names are otherwise the same in all witnesses (λύδιον, φρύγιον, δώριον, in that order).

apparatus.entry: ὑμέναιος H Par. V] ὑμεραῖος Bas.
apparatus.note: Bas. prints ὑμ + ερ-ligature + αῖ + ος-compendium, with a circumflex on αῖ. H V write ὑμέναιος, and V divides it ὑμέναι-|ος.

apparatus.entry: μεταφορᾷ οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων H Par. V] om. Bas.
apparatus.note: The full text in H Par. V reads: οὐ γὰρ τῇ τῶν διαστημάτων μόνῃ μεταφορᾷ, οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ … Bas. has only: τῇ τῶν διαστημάτων μόνῃ διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ. H spells it μεταφορᾶ … διαφορᾶι; Par. prints οὐδὲ as οὐ + δὲ-compendium. Claude's note on H 70r.1 considered μὲ διαφορὰ for the ετ-ligature, but no δ is visible; Par. and V confirm μεταφορᾷ. Mechanism: a skip from the first μόνῃ to the second would keep τούτων. In Par.'s lineation (27r.18–20), however, the words missing in Bas. are exactly those between the line-end syllables με- and δια-, so a compositor's single slip from one line end to the next is possible (see departures). A deliberate shortening in Bas. is the alternative. Par. shows that the editio princeps tradition had the full text.

apparatus.entry: σχολαιοτέραις H V] χολαιοτέραις Bas. Par.
apparatus.note: In H 70r.2 the αι of σχολαι- at the line end is retraced in darker ink, without any change of reading. Claude's note on Bas. describes the first sort as a σχ-ligature that looks like χ, but the established Bas. line reads χολαιοτέραις (see doubts). The non-word is in the apparatus because Bas. and Par. share it.

orthographica.Bas: Xylander's * before τὸ at 32.23 is not reproduced. Line-end divisions: ὑποδείγμα|τι is printed without a visible hyphen, and the τι of 32.25 is a ligature resembling π. ἐστὶ (33.3) is a compendium and is printed with a grave before the comma; normalised to ἐστί. διαφορὰς, at 33.9 keeps the grave before the comma. Bas. has μύρια (33.18), proparoxytone, which by the grammarians' distinction is the numeral 'ten thousand'. It is normalised to μυρία ('countless') with H Par. V; the sense 'countless and varied melodies' requires this. ποίκιλα (33.19) is an accent misprint, normalised to ποικίλα with H Par. V. ῥᾴδιον and ῥᾳδίως are printed with iota subscript. Πλάτων is capitalised. In the subscription Bas. prints Μουσικῆς with a capital and ends with a colon; the constituted text normalises it to Τέλος τῆς μουσικῆς (an editor may keep the capital, since it names the section). Commas after διαιρέσεις, διαφορὰς, γενναῖον, ἐξόδιος, μελῳδιῶν (33.13) and so on are dropped as not needed for the sense. ὑμεραῖος is in the apparatus, not here.
orthographica.H: Iota subscript is usually omitted: τῶ (τῷ, twice), συντακτικῶ, ἑκάστω, τῆ (τῇ, twice), μόνη (μόνῃ, twice), μεταφορᾶ; μελωδ- is written without iota throughout (δυσμελωδικώτατον 69v.9, μελω|δίας 69v.10–11, μελωδιῶν 69v.17–18, 69v.21–22, 70r.6). Iota adscript appears once: διαφορᾶι (70r.2). ῥάδιον and ῥαδίως are written without iota. Elision without an apostrophe: ἐφ ἑκάστω. The enclitic is accented: τὲ (70r.4). ἐστὶ. has a grave before the point. πλάτων is lower case. Abbreviations are expanded: (καὶ), π(ερὶ), γ(ὰρ), -(ων), -(ν), Τέλο(ς) τ(ῆ)ς μουσικ(ῆ)ς; the subscription is in red ink with a final colon. Punctuation is by high and low points. μυρία and ποικίλα are accented correctly. Claude's preliminary note on 69v.16 recorded πάν η ἕκαστον, but the established line reads πάλιν ἕκαστον, as in Bas. Par. V, so there is no variant. In παιήων (69v.20) the ω has a c-like left part; read as παιήων.
orthographica.Par: Acute before punctuation: ἐστί., διαφοράς,. Δυσμελῳδικώτατον has a capital after a high point. πλάτων is lower case. οὐδὲ is printed as οὐ + δὲ-compendium. μυρία and ποικίλα, are accented correctly, against Bas. Punctuation differs throughout (e.g. ἔρχεται, τὸ δὲ; παιήων· ὑμέναιος. ἐξόδιος.; ἁπλοῦν τε, καὶ; ποικίλα, κατασκευάζεται.). Subscription: Τέλος τῆς μουσικῆς·. χολαιοτέραις (shared with Bas.) is in the apparatus.
orthographica.V: The initial Δ of Δυσμελῳδικώτατον and the subscription τέλος τῆς μουσικῆς are in red ink (lower case, no point). Iota subscript is written in the established lines (τῷ, συντακτικῷ, ἑκάστῳ, τῇ, μόνῃ, μεταφορᾷ, διαφορᾷ). Claude's collator note reports μόνη μεταφορᾶ / διαφορᾶ without iota; either way this is only orthographic. Colons at period ends (καταστοχάζεσθαι:, κατασκευάζεται:). Commas: τούτων δὲ, πάλιν; νῦν δὲ, φρύγιον. ἐστὶ, has a grave before the comma. Πλάτων is capitalised. μυρία and ποικίλα are accented correctly. The dittography νῦν δὲ φρύγιον is in the apparatus.
orthographica.P: Not extant for this section: the file has no P fragment. Vincent's three extracts from BnF gr. 2448 do not reach these lines.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: τὸν ὅμοιον δὲ τρόπον … ἡ ἁρμονία συντάττει ('In the same way, harmonia arranges the remaining systems too')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: τὸν ὅμοιον γὰρ τρόπον … ('For in the same way, harmonia arranges the remaining systems too')
alternatives_for_translation.why: With γὰρ the sentence becomes a justification of what precedes: the enharmonic genus takes its name from ἁρμονία. That is possible, but the next sentence also begins with γὰρ, and δὲ gives the natural transition. For the translator: ἡ ἁρμονία here very probably means the enharmonic genus itself, its old name, as the preceding παρωνυμία-clause suggests, rather than 'harmonics' in general.

alternatives_for_translation.adopted: οὐ γὰρ τῇ τῶν διαστημάτων μόνῃ μεταφορᾷ, οὐδὲ τῇ μόνῃ τούτων διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ … ('not only by the shifting of the intervals, nor only by their difference, but also by …')
alternatives_for_translation.alternative: οὐ γὰρ τῇ τῶν διαστημάτων μόνῃ διαφορᾷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ … ('not by the difference of the intervals alone, but also by …')
alternatives_for_translation.why: The shorter text of Bas. is coherent, and it is the text of the 1556 Basel edition. Any rendering or quotation made from Bas. will lack the μεταφορά-clause, so the translator should not be surprised by the difference. The adopted text separates the transposition or shifting of intervals (behind the Lydian, Phrygian and Dorian melodies) from their difference (the genera).

resolved_doubts.issue: The established diplomatic line of Bas. reads χολαιοτέραις, and so does Par. Claude's own note on Bas. 33.15, however, describes the printed first sort as a σχ-ligature that 'resembles χ', with the reading σχολαιοτέραις. This changes only how Bas. is reported, not the constituted text, which is σχολαιοτέραις in either case.
resolved_doubts.options: (a) Bas. = χολαιοτέραις, as in the established line: the apparatus entry 'σχολαιοτέραις H V] χολαιοτέραις Bas. Par.' and the departure stand. (b) Bas. = σχολαιοτέραις with a σχ-ligature: the entry becomes 'σχολαιοτέραις Bas. H V] χολαιοτέραις Par.' and the departure is withdrawn.
resolved_doubts.evidence: Bas. line 33.15 as established, against bas_notes_claude p. 33 l. 15. Par. 27r.20 clearly has χολαιοτέραις, which makes (a) plausible, because Bas. often follows the printed tradition. The human editor should check the Bas. sort against the scan once more. I followed the established line, as instructed.
resolved_doubts.resolution: Resolved: Bas. prints χολαιοτέραις without σ (both checkers, high confidence; Par. also lacks σ). The entry «σχολαιοτέραις H V] χολαιοτέραις Bas. Par.» and the departure stand.
